targetText: Whatever the form of the process of production in a society, it must be a continuous process, must continue to go periodically through the same phases. A society can no more cease to produce than it can cease to consume. When viewed, therefore, as a connected whole, and as flowing on with incessant renewal, every social process of production is, at the same time, a process of reproduction.
explanation: Simple reproduction shows that capitalism continuously reproduces its own social conditions: workers leave production empty-handed and must return to sell their labor again.
